decision.question: Is the source mug visibly positioned to the right of the same headphones in the edited image; if not, is there reliable visual evidence of relevant attempted movement of the source mug, or reliable evidence that no relevant progress occurred?
decision.criteria: Pass only when visual evidence reliably establishes that the source mug itself is now positioned to the right of the same headphones. Fail when visual evidence reliably establishes either that relevant attempted movement occurred without fulfillment, or that no relevant progress toward the requested move occurred. For attempted movement, assess the source mug's former location and surrounding edited scene together; a conspicuous remnant or other visible changes may support attempted movement even if the right-side mug's identity cannot be established. Do not infer source-mug identity or fulfillment from color alone, from a mug being on the right, or from unrelated/newly generated mugs. A remnant counts as evidence of attempted movement only when its shape, position, and appearance reliably connect it to the source mug or otherwise clearly indicate a relevant edit. Use unknown when evidence cannot reliably establish fulfillment, attempted movement, or absence of progress. High confidence in uncertainty is not evidence that the requested edit is absent.
decision.binding: Compare the source image's large light-blue mug, including its body and handle, with the edited mugs, allowing for changes in appearance, scale, and lighting; compare the same headphones and assess whether the source mug is to their right. Separately inspect the source mug's former location and surrounding edited scene for reliable evidence of attempted movement, including the remnant's position, outline, and appearance and any other visible changes. Do not treat color alone, an indistinct blur, or a different-looking mug as proof of source-mug identity or progress. Keep attempted movement distinct from fulfillment: attempted movement without fulfillment is fail for this required condition; retain unknown if neither fulfillment nor relevant progress/no-progress can reliably be established.
